newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight interbank rate ends at 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight interbank rate ends at 10 pct.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate closed unchanged at 10 percent on Wednesday as the market remained short of funds, dealers said.
They said central Bank Negara was heard lending overnight funds at 11 percent through an agent bank.
"But Negara has been very selective in their lending," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
Earlier, one-month money was quoted at 10/12 percent against 9/10 percent on Tuesday.
One-week money was at 11/12 percent, against 13/15 percent.
Dealers said interbank rates remained high due to tight market liquidity.
"The market is still short of funds. Bank Negara is lending but only to selected finance and discount houses," another dealer said.
The liquidity squeeze followed heavy buying of the ringgit by the central bank last week to defend the ringgit from a speculative attack.
Although the actual size of the intervention was not known, dealers have estimated that between 2.5 billion and 5.0 billion ringgit was drained from the system.
Dealers said there was still confusion over where rates were heading.
Malaysia's Acting Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Tuesday the country did not favour a high interest rate regime.
But, the central bank was not doing much to help ease the market, dealers said.
"The ball is in Negara's court. It's a question of when they will pump in funds," one said.
Dealers said maturity of Bank Negara bills worth 500 million ringgit on Wednesday was not expected to have much impact on market liquidity.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were mixed to reflect the uncertainty over the direction of interbank rates.
At 0900 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up one point to 92.38, or an implied yield of 7.62 percent.
The December contract was down one to 92.62, or 7.38 percent.
Malaysian financial markets are closed on Thursday for Prophet Muhammad's birthday.
